sections.html:
Arlington is a compact, fully urban county facing Washington, D.C. over the Potomac. It covers about 26 square miles and counted 238,643 residents in 2020. Fairfax County, the City of Falls Church and the City of Alexandria border it, and no separate towns sit inside it.

Four Metro lines (Orange, Blue, Silver and Yellow) plus Interstates 395 and 66 serve the county. Shoppers think in neighborhoods: Rosslyn, Clarendon, Ballston, Pentagon City and Court House come up most. Every parcel is valued as of January 1, which makes the number on your January notice the place to begin with any tax question.

Real estate tax is billed in two equal halves. The first half is due June 15 and the second October 5. A payment made the next business day escapes the late penalty if the date falls on a weekend or holiday. State code puts the burden of knowing the dates on you, and a missing bill is no defense.

  • Escrow accounts mean your lender pays and no bill comes, unless the Treasurer's Office never receives the lender's payment.
  • If you sold and the buyer now owns the house, mail the bill back to the Treasurer's Office with whatever you know about the new owner.
  • Billing address changes go in writing to the Department of Real Estate Assessments.

State law sets the outer limits on late charges: a penalty up to 10 percent of the overdue tax (or $10, whichever is higher) and interest up to 10 percent a year.

sections.h2: The Arlington real estate tax rate
sections.html: The rate for calendar year 2025 was $1.033 per $100 of assessed value. Commercial property, including office buildings and hotels, carries an extra $0.125 per $100. The County Board sets the rate each April, so a later year can differ. Use the figure on your current bill rather than a number you find elsewhere.

New assessments take effect as of January 1 and are mailed and posted online each January. Fair market value, in the county's words, is the price a property would bring in a normal sale.

The county looks at a 12-month stretch of sales that begins 16 months before the effective date. For 2026 that stretch ran from September 1, 2024 through August 31, 2025. Since every sale in a neighborhood goes into the study, one odd sale moves your value only a little. A recent sale of your own house still counts, but as one data point among many.

Before listing, go through the notice carefully. Floor area, room counts and lot size should match the house. A wrong detail in the record is the simplest thing to correct with the neighborhood appraiser, and a corrected record means a fairer bill for whoever owns the house next.

Arlington offers four levels of appeal, and some can be skipped. Deadlines differ at each.

Appeal stepWhere to goTiming
Informal talkNeighborhood appraiser, 703-228-3920 or assessments@arlingtonva.usBefore you file anything
Department Review RequestDepartment of Real Estate AssessmentsEarly March: use the date printed on your notice
Board of EqualizationSeven county residents, appointed annuallyApril 15
Circuit Court1425 North Courthouse Road, 703-228-7010Final option

If April 1 arrives with no determination letter, file the Board of Equalization appeal anyway to protect your place. Going directly to the board is allowed, and it operates independently of the assessment office.

sections.h2: What a department review looks like
sections.html:
An appraiser calls to set up an inspection, usually of the inside and outside with a second appraiser along. The appraiser writes a recommendation, a supervisor reviews it, and the Director of Real Estate Assessments decides. You are told the outcome by mail or email. A review can lower the value, leave it alone or raise it, so back your case with comparable sales.

You can withdraw, or turn down the inspection, but then the review proceeds on the information the county already holds. When another person files on your behalf, the county wants a signed letter of authorization from the owner.

sections.h2: Tax relief for older and disabled owners
sections.html:
The Real Estate Tax Relief Program gives an exemption or a deferral to homeowners 65 and older and to owners who are totally and permanently disabled. Applications are due November 15, and a call to the county will confirm the date for the current cycle.

The county posted 2025 limits of annual income up to $105,937 and assets, leaving out the home, up to $499,709 for an exemption or $674,606 for a deferral. One more exemption is aimed at owners rated 100 percent service-connected, permanent and total, and a surviving spouse may also qualify. These limits are reset over time, so verify them before filing.

Work out who pays what before you reach the closing table. The Treasurer's Office tells owners to settle responsibility for the tax in the sale settlement, and the settlement attorney can explain how your contract handles it.

Virginia Code section 58.1-3340 makes the tax a lien on the real estate, ahead of other liens until paid, and the seller's share of the year is prorated by contract. For the deed itself, section 58.1-802 puts a grantor tax of fifty cents for every $500 of value on the seller in most deals, while section 58.1-801 sets the state recordation tax at 25 cents per $100.

Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure ahead of closing, and hand the paid receipt to the title company. If the buyer is taking over the bill, make sure the paperwork says so.

1. Read the January 1 value on your notice and compare it with the house.
  2. Call the neighborhood appraiser at 703-228-3920 if anything in the record looks wrong.
  3. Check which installments you have paid, since the June 15 and October 5 dates can fall on either side of a listing.
  4. Ask the settlement attorney how the year's tax will be split.
  5. Get a payoff figure from the Treasurer before you sign closing papers.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense in Arlington?
sections.html:
Cash can be the simpler route when a house needs repairs you would rather not fund, when taxes or a mortgage have slipped behind, or when you are moving away on a tight schedule. Two bills a year means a missed June or October installment can build quickly on a vacant house.

Measure any offer, ours included, against the county's January 1 value on your notice. We purchase houses in their current condition and put the offer in writing. Reach us by phone or text with the street address, and we will tell you what we can pay and how fast we can close.

faqs.q: When are Arlington County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: June 15 and October 5. Paying on the next business day avoids the penalty when a date falls on a weekend or holiday.

faqs.q: What was Arlington's real estate tax rate for 2025?
faqs.a: $1.033 per $100 of assessed value, plus $0.125 per $100 for commercial property. The County Board sets the rate each April.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal an Arlington assessment to the Board of Equalization?
faqs.a: April 15. Forms must be delivered, postmarked or filed online by midnight that day.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Arlington assessment?
faqs.a: The Department of Real Estate Assessments at 703-228-3920, at 2100 Clarendon Blvd, Suite 502. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and meetings are by appointment.

faqs.q: Can I get tax relief in Arlington if I am over 65?
faqs.a: Possibly. The Real Estate Tax Relief Program covers owners 65 and older and owners who are totally and permanently disabled, within income and asset limits. The filing deadline is November 15.
